transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lila Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Rivera (Redwood SE), Sofia Park (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Velox CTO), Tom Breen (Velox ML Eng), Nina Patel (Velox Security), Mark Li (Velox Product)

Summary:
Quick migration demo focused on API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood. Covered parameter mappings (temperature, top_p, stop tokens), streaming differences, function/tool calling equivalence, embeddings parity and idempotency, and private deployment considerations (VPC/KMS). Agreed next steps: parity spreadsheet, benchmark run, POC kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lila (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. I'm Lila from Redwood, I'm joined by Marco and Sofia on the engineering side. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Aisha (Velox CTO): Doing good, Lila. Thanks — excited to see the parity map, we've got a few constraints around latency and data residency.
[00:18] Tom (Velox ML Eng): Yeah, and we want to see how streaming and function calls map from our OpenAI usage.
[00:25] Lila: Great. Today's agenda — quick intro, then Marco will demo the Redwood API and console, show how we map calls from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together, talk about embeddings and optimize recommendations, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:35] Marco (Redwood SE): Cool. I'm going to share my screen — give me a sec — ok. So first, basic request parity. If you're using OpenAI's completion/chat endpoints, the body parameters map directly: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop — Redwood uses the same fields but we also add a routing policy param for dedicated vs hosted which you can pin at the SDK or request level.
[01:05] Tom: Wait, routing policy param? Is that in the header or body?
[01:10] Marco: Good call — it's a request header named x-redwood-route or an SDK arg. Example in the curl snippets we'll share. It controls region and capacity preference.
[01:18] Nina (Velox Security): For us, we need to pin requests to our VPC in the POC. Does that require anything special in the token or header?
[01:25] Sofia (Redwood SE): No special token change — you get a customer-specific endpoint for private deployments or a header-based routing flag for Dedicated. With Private (VPC) you will be calling a private endpoint inside your VPC, and we integrate with your KMS for key wrapping.
[01:40] Aisha: Good. Can you show an example of a streaming response? We rely a lot on partial tokens to render streaming UI.
[01:47] Marco: Yep — Redwood supports chunked HTTP streaming and websocket streaming. The semantics are similar to OpenAI's stream=1 where you get delta tokens in events. One caveat — we sometimes surface model variant warnings in-stream if we fall back to a lower-cost model during capacity spikes.
[02:10] Mark (Velox Product): Model fallback warnings — will that break our UI? We can't show inconsistent responses to users.
[02:16] Lila: We have config to suppress those warnings or to auto-retry with a different routing preference. For production you can configure an SLO-based fallback policy — either fail closed or return a 503 and let your app retry. We'll send the config docs.
[02:30] Tom: Ok, on emeddings — our pipeline uses embeddings from Anthropic and OpenAI interchangeably. How close are Redwood embeddings? Vector dimensionality? Idempotency?
[02:40] Sofia: Embeddings parity depends on the model you pick. We host curated open models with verified dims, and we also provide a drop-in mapping table: for example, anth-embed-large -> redwood-embed-a1 (1536 dims) with similarity thresholds we've measured. We include a 'distance shift' note in the sheet so you can adjust nearest neighbor thresholds.
[03:05] Tom: So you provide a numeric mapping and recommended similarity cutoff?
[03:08] Sofia: Exactly. We'll provide the spreadsheet with measured MRR and recall on your sample prompts if you give us a set.
[03:15] Aisha: About billing — how granular is cost visibility? We need token-level cost breakdown by route and model.
[03:22] Lila: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route, per-model breakdowns, and you can export CSVs. For Dedicated customers we also show burst usage and reserved capacity utilization.
[03:32] Nina: For audits we need audit logs and SSO integration — can you pull logs into our SIEM?
[03:38] Marco: Yes. We provide structured audit logs, syslog/forwarding, and long retention packages. SAML SSO and RBAC are supported. For Private customers we can ship logs to your S3 or the SIEM endpoint.
[03:52] Aisha: Awesome. Now, compatibility pain points — where do folks trip up when migrating from OpenAI or Anthropic?
[03:58] Marco: Two common places: 1) stop token differences and tokenizer edge-cases causing minor token count diffs; 2) streaming vs function calling differences — Anthropic's style of function calling isn't identical, so you need small adapter logic. Also, quantization/latency tradeoffs — on some model variants we recommend 4-bit quantization but test quality first.
[04:25] Tom: About function calling — does Redwood do automatic function calling like newer OpenAI models?
[04:30] Sofia: We support structured function/tool calling. Our schema format is near-identical to OpenAI's recent spec; for Anthropic/Together you might need a mapping layer. We'll include adapter snippets in Python/Node.
[04:44] Mark: Are there SDKs? We use node on frontend and python in backend.
[04:47] Lila: Yep — official SDKs for Node and Python. Snippets in the parity sheet will be in curl, node, python.
[04:54] [05:00] Marco: Now I'll demo a quick migration example — show a three-line curl from OpenAI and the equivalent Redwood call.
[05:10] Marco: (screen) OpenAI call: curl openai... prompt..., temperature 0.2, max_tokens 256. Redwood: replace endpoint to api.redwood.ai/v1/complete, same params; add x-redwood-route if you want dedicated. Same response envelope, but we add meta.routing and timing fields.
[05:35] Tom: Are there header differences for rate limit headers? We rely on X-Rate-Limit-Remaining.
[05:40] Marco: We expose x-rw-rate-limit and x-rw-remaining; mapping will be in the docs. Some header names differ but we keep same semantics.
[05:50] Aisha: On the security side, how is data at rest encrypted and how do we prove keys are customer controlled?
[05:57] Sofia: For Private deployments we integrate with your KMS and can use customer-managed keys. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with KMS-backed keys and a SOC2-attested process. We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
[06:12] Nina: Do you support HSM integrations?
[06:14] Marco: Yes — HSM via standard KMS connectors; we'll note supported vendors in the security pack.
[06:20] Tom: Performance — our SLA is focused on sub-200ms p99 for short prompts. Do you have p99 numbers for similar customers?
[06:28] Marco: On hosted for smaller models we can hit 100-150ms p99 for single-token latencies, but depends on batch behavior and KV cache hit rates. Dedicated pools give more predictable numbers. For p99 across a 2k token prompt it's higher — we'll run the benchmark on your workload to give exacts.
[06:50] Lila: This is where Redwood Optimize helps — intelligent batching and KV cache recommendations to meet latency SLOs while lowering per-token cost.
[06:58] Mark: Can Optimize suggest quantization levels?
[07:00] Sofia: Yes. It suggests model variants and quantization profiles (e.g., 4-bit/8-bit) per workload with expected quality delta estimates.
[07:10] [07:30] Tom: For our POC we'll need to reproduce our current cost-per-1M tokens comparison across OpenAI+Anthropic vs Redwood. Will you help compute that?
[07:36] Lila: Absolutely — Marco will run a 50k token benchmark using your prompts and then we'll extrapolate. We'll include cost-model assumptions in the spreadsheet.
[07:45] Aisha: One more — data residency. We're in health; we need EU-only storage for certain tenants. Is regional pinning supported?
[07:54] Marco: Yes. You can pin models/requests to specific regions, and Private allows on-prem control. We'll document region tags and the routing policy.
[08:05] Nina: Any known gotchas with KV cache and session affinity? We rely on long conversations and need consistent KV cache availability.
[08:12] Sofia: You can pin sessions to the same pool using sticky routing keys or session tokens. If you use Dedicated it's simpler — the pool maintains your KV cache. On hosted we have a distributed cache with best-effort locality, but for strict affinity Private is recommended.
[08:30] Tom: Regarding tokenization — slight diffs feed into costs and chunking. Do you expose tokenizer tooling so we can match token counts?
[08:36] Marco: Yep — SDK includes tokenizer utilities and a lighthouse tool that simulates token usage across payloads so you can map cost accurately.
[08:45] [09:00] Mark: Can we do a quick look at the console for rollouts and observability?
[09:05] Marco: Sure — console screenshot. You can see per-route latency, token cost, and error traces. Rollouts section shows canary percentages and automatic fallback policies.
[09:25] Lila: We often advise starting with a small canary on Redwood hosted with autoscaling, then move to Dedicated if you need predictability.
[09:34] Aisha: Pricing model question — is hosted pay-as-you-go then switch to reserved capacity for Dedicated?
[09:40] Lila: Exactly — hosted usage-based, Dedicated is reserved monthly/annual with burst add-ons. We'll include ballpark pricing for both.
[09:50] Nina: Compliance — will you provide a shared responsibility matrix for Private vs Hosted?
[09:55] Sofia: Yes, included in the security pack. We'll highlight network boundaries, data retention, and roles.
[10:05] [10:30] Tom: A few nitty-gritty questions: 1) are model outputs deterministic if we set temperature=0? 2) do you guarantee same output ordering with top_p?
[10:38] Marco: Determinism depends on the model itself and quantization. For temp=0 we get high determinism but not absolute; we'll surface randomness seeds if you need exact bit-level repeatability. For top_p, ordering of tokens follows model sampling; slight differences can exist between model variants.
[10:58] Aisha: Ok, sounds reasonable. Any limitations on attachments or multimodal?
[11:05] Sofia: Currently primary focus is text and embeddings; we have roadmap items for multimodal with partner models, and we'll share timelines if that matters.
[11:15] Lila: Wrapping up — recap of agreed items: we'll send parity mapping spreadsheet, SDK snippets, SOC2/security docs, and run a benchmark on your prompt set. Then schedule a POC kickoff next week.
[11:30] Mark: Sounds good. Nina — any final security must-haves?
[11:35] Nina: Just the questionnaire and verification of KMS/HSM options and log retention. I'll send that list.
[11:42] Lila: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[11:46] Aisha: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
